#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from LSF
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch --job-name="process_reuters_lda_data_train[1-10]" --array=1-10 script.sh
#
# Alternatively, submit individual jobs in a loop:
# for i in {1..10}; do
#   flux batch --job-name="process_reuters_lda_data_train[$i]" --env=FLUX_TASK_ID=$i script.sh
# done

# Original queue: airoldi
# Note: Flux does not have queues/partitions in the same way as LSF
# Queue selection and priority are managed through Flux's scheduling policies
# Performance impact: Job prioritization depends on site-specific Flux configuration
# Consult your site's Flux documentation for equivalent resource pools or banks

# Email notification: jbischof@fas.harvard.edu
# Note: Flux does not have built-in email notification directives
# Performance impact: User must manually monitor job status or implement external
# monitoring solutions using flux job events or flux watch commands

# Job Array: process_reuters_lda_data_train[1-10]
# Note: Flux supports job arrays via --array flag at submission time
# Use: flux batch --array=1-10 script.sh
# Array index is available via ${FLUX_TASK_ID} environment variable
# (LSF uses ${LSB_JOBINDEX})

# THE COMMAND TO GIVE TO R, CHANGE TO THE APPROPRIATE FILENAME:
partition=train
cutoff=500

# Replace LSB_JOBINDEX with FLUX_TASK_ID for Flux job arrays
main_dir=/n/airoldifs2/lab/jbischof/reuters_output/mmm_folds/fold${FLUX_TASK_ID}/
out_dir=${main_dir}mmm_raw_data/parsed_${partition}_data${cutoff}/

# Create partition directory if doesn't already exist
if [ ! -d $out_dir ]
then
   mkdir $out_dir
fi

# Run python script
python ../process_parse_lda_data.py $partition $cutoff $main_dir

issues: The script correctly documents that Flux does not support in-script resource directives and provides proper submission command syntax in comments.
The script properly replaces LSF's ${LSB_JOBINDEX} with Flux's ${FLUX_TASK_ID} for job array indexing.

No explicit resource requests are specified. The script will run with default resources (typically 1 node, 1 core). If the Python script requires specific CPU, memory, or time limits, these should be specified at submission time using: flux batch -N <nodes> -n <tasks> -c <cores-per-task> --time-limit=<duration> --array=1-10 script.sh

The alternative submission method shown in comments (using a loop with --env=FLUX_TASK_ID=$i) is not the standard way to submit job arrays in Flux. The --array flag automatically sets FLUX_TASK_ID, so manually setting it via --env is redundant and could cause confusion.
Consider adding resource specifications in the submission command documentation, e.g., 'flux batch --array=1-10 -n 1 -c 1 --time-limit=1h script.sh' to ensure adequate resources.
The script assumes FLUX_TASK_ID will be set by the job array mechanism. If the script is submitted without --array flag, FLUX_TASK_ID will be undefined, causing the paths to be malformed.
Consider adding a check at the beginning: 'if [ -z "${FLUX_TASK_ID}" ]; then echo "Error: Must submit as job array"; exit 1; fi'
